Compose an API, MVC website and SQL Server

Read the Compose file and start the three services together.

Open interactive lesson and complete code

What you are building

A student website, API and database running in containers

Package a .NET API and MVC website into images. Docker Compose starts them with SQL Server so the three services can work together.

SQL Server stores its files in a named Docker volume so they can survive container replacement.

Check the result

Follow the setup steps, start the Compose stack, open the website and add a student.

Compose is a set of instructions for several containers that belong together. Our stack has a website, an API and SQL Server.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Prepare your computer

Install Docker Desktop with Linux containers enabled and the .NET10 SDK. For the full SQL Server stack use supported x64 hardware with enough memory for SQL Server. WPF does not run in the Linux ASP.NET image. Accept applicable vendor licences yourself during installation. Run docker version and docker compose version in a terminal; start Docker Desktop if the engine cannot be reached.

Before the first start

Download the complete stack. It contains Api, Website, compose.yaml and .env.example. Copy .env.example to .env in the root folder. Replace the demonstration password with your own strong local password. Do not commit .env. In Api generate InitialCreate with dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate before building the images. The classroom API applies those migrations when StudyLabMigrate=true. 

docker compose config --quiet
docker compose up --build -d
docker compose ps
docker compose logs api

Follow the startup order

db starts SQL Server Developer edition and stores files in school-data. Its sqlcmd healthcheck must succeed before api starts. api retries transient database connections and performs its classroom migration. website starts after the API container is started; that is not the same as API readiness, so wait for the API migration to finish in logs before opening the website.

Test every tier

Open http://localhost:5100/health, then http://localhost:5100/api/students, then http://localhost:5200. Expected: a ready health response, an empty list on a new database, then an MVC form. Create Lefa,22 in the website. The website calls api; api writes a SQL Server row. Read, update and delete through the form. Keep a row for the volume test.

Try it yourself

Why use db,1433 instead of localhost inside api?

Worked answer

localhost inside api means the API container itself. Compose DNS resolves db to the database service.

Is depends_on:service_started enough to prove SQL Server can accept connections?

Worked answer

No. The database uses a healthcheck and service_healthy condition, plus transient retry handling.
